SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: The bivariate correlations (i.e., standardized βs) between intelligence and ideational fluency were r = .56 (p b .01, n = 21) below the breakpoint of 86.09 IQ points and r = .09 (ns, n = 275) above it. For creative potential assessed by means of the Top 2 originality score, a significant breakpoint was detected at an IQ of 104.00 points (p b .05; 95% CI = 93.07–114.90 points). The bivariate correlations between intelligence and creative potential were r = .38 (p b .01, n = 121) below the breakpoint and r = .14 (ns, n = 175) above it. When the average originality was considered as a criterion, a significant correlation between intelligence and creative potential was obtained for the lower IQ range (r = .35, p b .01, n = 232), but not for the upper IQ range (r = −.01, ns, n = 65).

The arithmetic mean for Top 2 originality score is (0.38 + 0.14) / 2 = 0.26. section_summary.extract_value: This section details segmented regression analyses performed for three criteria of creative potential (ideational fluency, Top 2 originality score, average originality) and for creative achievement. For ideational fluency, a breakpoint was found at IQ 86.09, with correlations of r = .56 (n=21) below and r = .09 (n=275) above. For Top 2 originality, a breakpoint was at IQ 104.00, with correlations of r = .38 (n=121) below and r = .14 (n=175) above. For average originality, a non-significant breakpoint was estimated at IQ 119.60, showing correlations of r = .35 (n=232) for the lower IQ range and r = −.01 (n=65) for the upper range. No significant breakpoint was detected for creative achievement.
